risks: Low for patients (no change to care beyond prompting conversations); possible distress for bereaved families contacted after a death.
consent: Waiver of consent requested for chart review of triggered patients; bereaved families receive an invitation letter and may decline any contact; consent is implied by return of the questionnaire, with a telephone option only if the family opts in.
data: Extracted notes are pseudonymised; quality ratings stored without names; family responses kept separate from clinical data.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: families of younger patients, in deprived neighbourhoods and with limited English respond least. Telephone and online routes, translated letters and response reporting by deprivation address this; the template prompts apply to all triggered patients regardless of diagnosis.
effectiveness: Success is meeting the progression criteria, not showing an effect.
efficiency: Two wards instead of six keep costs within the grant.
costs: Analyst time, rater time, postage and printing within the internal grant.
grants: A positive feasibility result would support an external grant application for the stepped-wedge trial.
partnerships: Ward managers, the record build team, the bereavement service and two bereaved family members as partners.
rebPath: Research ethics board review as minimal risk with a waiver of consent for chart review, following TCPS 2; the bereavement service advises on the timing and wording of family contact.
limitations: Two wards; no comparison group; small numbers of families.
summary: Minimal-risk feasibility study with a chart review waiver and careful family contact.
